tagline: Rice towns and an old beach above the marsh.
intro: From Hayes on Bayou Lacassine, the drive runs through the rice country of Gueydan and on to Abbeville, where the Vermilion River passes through downtown. Farther along lies Pecan Island. The ground there is an old beach, made of shells and sand and surrounded by coastal marsh.

Water gave these places their boundaries and their work. At Gueydan, irrigation helped turn land dismissed by surveyors as sea marsh into rice country; at Pecan Island, prehistoric beach ridges hold the settlement above the marsh.

moments.title: Hayes
moments.text: In 1905, after the railroad came and the population shifted, the Methodist church building was loaded onto a logging wagon and moved into Hayes.

moments.title: Gueydan
moments.text: The first irrigation pump in Louisiana was built nearby at Primeaux Landing, and rice spread across land surveyors had written off as sea marsh, unfit for cultivation.

moments.title: Pecan Island
moments.text: Two prehistoric beach ridges meet beneath the community, leaving an old shoreline surrounded by marsh.
